about_thesis: This application was developed as part of a bachelor's thesis at Aalen University.
about_goal: The goal of the project was to provide a user-friendly and interactive visualization of the Dijkstra algorithm, specifically suitable for didactic use in lectures and exercises.
about_functionality: The application allows users to understand the functionality of the Dijkstra algorithm through step-by-step explanations and color highlights directly in the graph.
about_usage: Learners and teachers can use both predefined and self-created graphs to explore and apply the algorithm.
about_technology: The project is based on the Python library Shiny for Python, combined with NetworkX for graph representation and analysis.
about_research: The development of the application was guided by best practices from research on algorithm visualization.
about_connection: The project exemplifies the connection between computer science and pedagogy and offers an innovative solution for conveying complex algorithmic concepts.
about_source: You can find the sourcecode for this App on https://github.com/Timo4D/Dijkstra
dijkstra_sources_intro: I don not own any of this content but these sources can provide you with more Information's about the Dijkstra Algorithm

dijkstra_step_0: 0. Algorithm is initialized with distance 0 for the start node and ∞ (infinite) for all other nodes
dijkstra_step_1: 1. The current node is selected from the unvisited vertices by the shortest distance from the start
dijkstra_step_2: 2. For the current node, provisional distances to all neighboring vertices are calculated / updated
dijkstra_step_3: 3. Repeat (from 1.) or stop, when the provisional distance to the destination node is less than or equal to the shortest distance to an unvisited node.
tutorial_welcome_content: This interactive tutorial will guide you through all the features of the Dijkstra algorithm visualizer. You can navigate using the buttons below or skip this tutorial entirely.
tutorial_graph_selection_content: Start by choosing a graph type. You can select from Germany Example (simple city network), Random Graph (customizable network), Import from Edgelist (define your own edges), or Upload a CSV file.
tutorial_prediction_game_content: Toggle this switch to enable Prediction Game Mode! When active, you'll be challenged to predict which node Dijkstra will visit next, earning points for correct predictions.
tutorial_prediction_game_action: Try toggling this switch on and off.
tutorial_graph_settings_content: Depending on your graph selection, different settings will appear here. For Random Graph, you can adjust the number of nodes, neighbors, and rewiring probability. For edge lists, you can define custom connections.
tutorial_graph_settings_action: These settings change based on your graph selection above.
tutorial_start_node_content: Choose which node the algorithm should start from. This will be highlighted in green on the graph visualization.
tutorial_start_node_action: Try changing this number to select different starting points.
tutorial_target_node_content: Choose the destination node that Dijkstra should find the shortest path to. This will be highlighted in red on the graph.
tutorial_target_node_action: Set this to a different node than your start node.
tutorial_algorithm_controls_content: Use these buttons to step through the Dijkstra algorithm. 'Next Step' advances the algorithm one step forward, while 'Previous Step' lets you go back to review earlier steps.
tutorial_algorithm_controls_action: These buttons become active once you have a valid graph setup.
tutorial_distances_table_content: This table shows the current shortest known distances from the start node to all other nodes. As the algorithm progresses, these values get updated when shorter paths are discovered.
tutorial_distances_table_action: Watch how these values change as you step through the algorithm.
tutorial_visited_nodes_content: This card shows which nodes the algorithm has already processed. Once a node is visited, its shortest path has been finalized.
tutorial_visited_nodes_action: Visited nodes appear here as the algorithm progresses.
tutorial_algorithm_explanation_content: This section provides detailed explanations of what's happening at each step of the algorithm, helping you understand the logic behind Dijkstra's method.
tutorial_algorithm_explanation_action: Step-by-step explanations appear here during execution.
tutorial_ready_content: You're now ready to use PathSolver! Start by selecting a graph, setting your start and target nodes, then use the Next Step button to watch Dijkstra find the shortest path. Have fun exploring!

algorithm_start_message: 🚀 Starting Dijkstra's algorithm! First set distance to start node to 0 and every other node to infinity
graph_not_connected: ❌ Cannot run Dijkstra algorithm: The graph is not fully connected!
connected_graph_required: A connected graph is required for Dijkstra's algorithm to find paths between all nodes. This graph has isolated components that cannot reach each other.
generate_new_graph: • Generate a new random graph, or
add_edges: • Add edges to connect all components, or
choose_connected: • Choose a different graph that is fully connected
start_node_not_exist: Start node {start_node} does not exist in the graph. Available nodes: {nodes}
target_node_not_exist: Target node {target_node} does not exist in the graph. Available nodes: {nodes}
examining_neighbors: 🔍 Now examining neighbors of node {current_node} (visited {nodes_visited_count} nodes so far)
calculate_neighbor_costs: You need to calculate the cost of all unvisited neighbours. To do this add the distance to your current node + the weight of the edge.
update_if_lower: If the weight is lower than what's already calculated we need to update it, otherwise we won't change it
exclude_visited_nodes: We will leave nodes {nodes_visited_without_current} out as we have already visited them
selected_lowest_cost_node: ✅ Selected node {node} (lowest unvisited cost) as our new current node.
continue_algorithm: 🔄 Since {node} is not our target node, we'll continue the algorithm by examining its neighbors next.
algorithm_progress: Progress: {visited}/{total} nodes visited. This is the core of Dijkstra's algorithm: repeatedly select the unvisited node with minimum distance and explore its neighbors.
start_node_lookup_not_found: Start node {start_node} (lookup: {lookup}) not found in distance table
invalid_nodes_in_solution: Invalid nodes: {invalid_nodes}. Please only use nodes that exist in the graph.
no_edge_between_nodes: No edge exists between nodes {node1} and {node2}. Please check your path.
prediction_game_question: 🎮 Prediction Game: Which node will Dijkstra visit next?
prediction_game_instructions: Look at the unvisited nodes in the distance table and click on the one with the lowest cost in the graph above!
target_reached: We have now arrived at our Target node, that means we are done and have found the shortest possible distance to it
enter_solution: You now have to enter your solution of the fastest path in new Box below. If it is correct you will see the path on the graph.
enter_positive_number: Please enter a positive number for the weight.
cannot_delete_min_nodes: Cannot delete node: Graph must have at least 2 nodes
cannot_delete_disconnect: Cannot delete edge {source}-{target}: This would disconnect the graph
created_edge: Created edge between nodes {source} and {target} with weight 1
cannot_create_invalid_nodes: Cannot create edge: Invalid nodes {source} or {target}
cannot_update_nonexistent: Cannot update weight: Edge {source}-{target} does not exist
added_new_node: Added new node {node_id} to the graph at position ({x}, {y})
edge_creation_start: Edge creation mode: Selected source node {source}. Right-click on another node to connect.
select_k_not_smaller_n: Please select make sure that k is not smaller than n
